title: What happens when the first digit is bigger?
description: The number trick is tried on eighty three, whose first digit is bigger. Letters show that taking the reverse away from the number gives nine times the gap between the digits, so nine still divides it. Keeko doubts this and thinks the digits should be added.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the first digit is larger, subtract the reverse from the number and the nines still group together. Watch for students who add the digits instead of taking the smaller from the larger.

source: Take 83, whose first digit is bigger. Follow the trick and s
video_script.why: The child sees that the same letters work when the first digit is the larger one, and the result is still nine times the gap between the digits.
video_script.substitution: Write the number as 10a + b and its reverse as 10b + a with a larger than b, subtract the reverse from the number, group the nines, and check with 83.
video_script.anchor: the number 83 and its reverse 38 on the board, then the same two numbers written with letters
video_script.wrong_answer: nine times the sum of the digits
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the digits eight and three to get eleven and says the result is nine times the sum of the digits, which would be ninety nine, instead of taking the smaller digit from the larger.
video_script.payoff_line: Nine still divides the result, which is nine times the larger digit take away the smaller digit

final_answer.spoken: nine times eigh take away bee

maths_rules: 83 = 10 × 8 + 3; a number with digits a and b is 10a + b; the reverse is 10b + a; a > b
9a − 9b = 9 × (a − b), so the result is divisible by 9
slip: 9 × (8 + 3) = 99 is not 45, so the digits are not added
video_script.design: One idea: when the first digit is larger the working turns around, the reverse is taken from the number, and the nines still group together. The number and its reverse stay on the board. Keeko's doubt is to add the digits.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the number 83 written, its reverse 38, and 83 − 38 = 45, 45 ÷ 9 = 5

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: the words every such number? appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is from your book. It asks what happens if the first digit is bigger.
<bookmark mark='pick'/>Take eighty three and reverse the digits to get thirty eight.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Eighty three take away thirty eight is forty five. Nine divides forty five five times, with nothing left over.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Will nine divide the result for every number like this?

beats.on_screen: the numbers stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 83 = 10 × 8 + 3, and 8 is larger than 3; letters: number = 10a + b with a larger than b

marks.tens: 83 splits into 10 × 8 and 3, and 8 is marked larger
marks.letters: the digits become the letters a and b, and the number becomes 10a + b
marks.order: the number is marked as the larger one and the reverse as the smaller one

beats.colours: tens part and ones part in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='tens'/>Eighty three is eight tens and three ones, so its first digit is larger.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>Use letters, with eigh in the tens place and bee in the ones place. Eigh is larger than bee.
<bookmark mark='order'/>This time the number is the larger one. We take the reverse away from it.

beats.on_screen: Given: a two digit number with tens digit a and ones digit b, different digits, a larger than b

marks.given: the number and its digits are written with letters

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a two digit number with eigh in the tens place and bee in the ones place. The digits are different, and eigh is larger.

beats.on_screen: To show: the number take away its reverse is divisible by 9

marks.find: the aim is written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to show that nine divides the number take away its reverse.

marks.num: 10a + b is written for the number
marks.rev: 10b + a is written for the reverse

narration: <bookmark mark='num'/>Step one, write both numbers by place value. The number is ten times eigh plus bee.
<bookmark mark='rev'/>The reverse is ten times bee plus eigh.

marks.group: the a terms and the b terms are grouped

beats.colours: the a terms and the b terms in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step two, take the reverse away from the number. That is ten eigh plus bee, take away ten bee plus eigh.
<bookmark mark='group'/>Group the eighs and the bees.
<bookmark mark='nines'/>Ten eigh take away eigh is nine eigh. Bee take away ten bee is minus nine bee.

marks.common: the common 9 is pulled out in front
marks.div: the words 9 divides it are written

beats.colours: the common 9 in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='common'/>Step three, take out nine, because both parts have nine. Nine eigh take away nine bee is nine times eigh take away bee.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Nine is a factor of the result, so nine divides it.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check with 83: a − b = 8 − 3 = 5 and 9 × 5 = 45
narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step four, check with eighty three. Eigh take away bee is eight take away three, which is five.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Nine times five is forty five, the same as before.

beats.on_screen: Answer: result = 9 × (a − b), still divisible by 9

marks.ans: the answer result = 9 × (a − b) is boxed
marks.gap: a − b glows as the digit gap

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Nine still divides the result, which is nine times the larger digit take away the smaller digit.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Again the result is nine times the gap between the two digits of the number.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the numbers
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 9 × (8 + 3) = 99; 83 − 38 = 45 appears beside it and 99 is struck out

marks.fix: the gap 8 − 3 glows in place of 8 + 3

beats.colours: the wrong idea in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the result is nine times the sum of the digits. Eight plus three is eleven, so that would be ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='test'/>But the real result is only forty five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The digits are not added, because we take the smaller digit from the larger one.
